title: Natural Resources
seo_title: Grade 7 Natural Resources Worksheets: Oil, Coal, Minerals and Groundwater
standard_text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth's mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on natural resources (NGSS MS-ESS3-1): how oil, coal, metal ores and groundwater form, why they are unevenly distributed, and how long limited resources last. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Resources are where geologic processes put them.
key_sub: Oil formed from buried sea life, coal from ancient swamps, and ores near volcanoes, so resources are uneven and limited.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's mineral, energy and groundwater resources are not spread evenly. They are found where geologic processes concentrated them, long ago or today.

  • Oil and natural gas: from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years.
  • Coal: from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years.
  • Copper and gold ores: from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries.
  • Groundwater: from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers).
  • Rock salt: from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago.
  • Iron ore: from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers.

Most of these resources form over millions of years, so they are nonrenewable on human time scales. Groundwater can be used up if it is pumped faster than rain refills it.

Example

Where would you look for oil?

Oil forms from buried marine organisms.

Answer: in sedimentary rock that was once under the sea

Example

An oil field has 600 million barrels and 30 million are used a year. How long will it last?

600 ÷ 30

Answer: 20 years

Common mistakes

  • Thinking oil comes from dinosaurs.
  • Thinking resources are spread evenly everywhere.
  • Thinking minerals and fossil fuels are replaced quickly.

faq.q: Why are resources like oil and metals found only in some places?
faq.a: They formed only where certain geologic processes happened, such as buried marine sediments for oil or magma and hot water for metal ores.
From tiny marine organisms buried in sediment and changed by heat and pressure over millions of years.
Yes. If people pump water out of an aquifer faster than rain refills it, the water level drops and wells can dry up.

items.q: Why do some countries have lots of oil and others have none?
c: Oil forms only where specific conditions existed in the past.
items.e: Geologic history determines where resources are.
